title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 29
paragraphs: Bearing a grudge, then, on both these counts, the Thessalians sent a herald and addressed the Phokians as follows: “Phokians, we advise you to be more inclined now to change your minds and admit that you are not on a level with us. In former times, so long as it pleased us to be on that side, we always held the advantage over you among the Greeks; and now we have such great influence with the barbarian that it rests with us to cause you to be stripped of your land and sold into slavery. But though we have all the power in our hands, we do not bear malice: pay us fifty talents of silver in exchange for this, and we undertake to avert the dangers threatening to come upon your land.”
